To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) a new method for multi agent reinforcement learning, AI QMIX, can generalize across dynamic scenarios and 2 ) AI QMIX can learn to share knowledge across variable sized scenarios by using an attention mechanism and 3) AI QMIX learns to generalize across different types of agents and entities by using a training objective that imagines sub scenarios.

we propose Attentive Imaginary QMIX, a novel method for dynamic multi agent reinforcement learning that learns to combine sub group behaviors in order to improve generalization across variable sized scenarios with varying agent types and quantities.

1) an agent's ability to imagine sub scenarios and share model parameters between scenarios with different agent/entity combinations is crucial to generalizing across variable sized scenarios in MARL, and 2) the ability to learn from sub scenarios can improve the learning of the optimal team behaviors in these scenarios.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of dynamic MARL, where agents need to learn to interact with varying quantities and combinations of agents and non-agent entities, in order to achieve a given task.
the problem of multi-agent reinforcement learning (MAR-L), where a team of agents must cooperate to achieve a common goal.
the problem of dynamic multi agent reinforcement learning, where the quantity and/or types of agents and non agents in the environment are not known a priori, and must be generalized over.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have introduced a novel MARL method for dynamic environments and demonstrated its effectiveness on a variety of environments.
the proposed approach is a novel and effective method for learning dynamic multi agent tasks that generalizes across a combinatorially large number of task configurations.
our method Attentive Imaginitive QMIX (AI-QMIX) is a novel and effective approach that can learn to generalize across dynamic configurations of multi agent tasks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we propose a novel method for multi agent reinforcement learning in dynamic scenarios that generalizes across variable quantities and types of agent and non agent entities, outperforming state of the art methods for dynamic MARL on both a grid world and a modified version of the Starcraft Multi Agent Challenge.

, in dynamic multi agent tasks with variable quantities of agents/entities, the optimal behavior for a given scenario can be decomposed into sub group relationships that can be combined to form the team level behavior, and that our proposed method can effectively capture and utilize these sub group patterns to improve generalization across variable scenarios.
